notes:
BAHRAIN (settled, filed). Read the consolidated English text of Law No. (64) of 2006 promulgating the Central Bank of Bahrain and Financial Institutions Law, published by Bahrain's Legislation & Legal Opinion Commission (lloc.gov.bh/FullEn/K6406.docx, 'Published on the website on May 2024', incorporating Law 34/2015 and Law 21/2016). Qualifying provisions: Art 5 (Board of seven, including a representative of the Ministry of Finance, all appointed by Royal Decree for four-year renewable terms, the appointing Decree naming the Chairman and Vice Chairman); Art 10 (Governor, of ministerial rank, appointed by Royal Decree for a renewable five-year term; Deputy Governor likewise); Art 173 (the Minister monitors the Bank's adherence to the general economic policy of the Kingdom; where the Minister finds a conflict and the Board insists on its opinion, the Minister refers the conflict to the Cabinet, which resolves it by an order issued within thirty days). The promulgating Decree 64/2006 (cbb.gov.bh PDF, also read) is dated 6 September 2006 and comes into effect the day after publication. Rejected as non-qualifying in the same law: Art 173(a)-(b) reporting and information duties, and Art 9 (termination of Board membership only on stated grounds, on the Board's own recommendation) - ordinary accountability, not capture.

OMAN (settled, filed). Read the Banking Law issued by Royal Decree 114/2000, English PDF on the Central Bank of Oman's own site (cbo.gov.om/sites/assets/Documents/English/LawRegulations/BankingLaw.pdf), via WebFetch because curl could not verify that host's TLS chain. Qualifying: Art 8(b) and Art 11(a) (all seven governors of the Board appointed by His Majesty the Sultan for five-year terms, the Sultan designating the Chairman and Deputy Chairman); Art 9 (one governor is a representative of the Ministry of Finance); Art 21(a) (Executive President appointed by Royal Decree); Art 41(a) ('The par value of the Rial Omani shall be determined from time to time by His Majesty the Sultan'); Art 31 (the external reserve ratio set by the Board subject to the Sultan's approval). Document states it was issued 17 Ramadan 1421H / 13 December 2000 and published in Official Gazette No. 685 of 16/12/2000, effective from the date of publication, so the date filed is 2000-12-16. NOT relied on: Art 13 removal of a governor, which has stated grounds and runs on the Board's own recommendation. Caveat for the caller: law-firm commentary found in search (trowers.com, cms.law) says Oman revamped its Banking Law by a new Royal Decree in 2024/2025; the 2000 law is what CBO itself still publishes in English at the above URL, and the record names it as such, but someone may want to check whether a successor decree has replaced these articles.

CAMBODIA (settled, filed). Read the English text of the Law on the Organization and Conduct of the National Bank of Cambodia, promulgated 26 January 1996, on the Cambodian government library (lib.ncdd.gov.kh/storage/app/public/test_library/CAT_17589_1/1996-Function-NBC-en.pdf) via WebFetch; curl to that host returned 403 Forbidden. Qualifying: Art 13 (the Governor and Deputy Governor are 'appointed, replaced and dismissed by a royal decree on the recommendation of the Royal Government', with no stated grounds; other Board members appointed, replaced and dismissed by sub-decree); Art 12(1) (the seven-member Board includes a representative of the Ministry of Economy and Finance and a representative of the head of the Royal Government); Art 45 (withdrawing or calling in currency requires the Royal Government's consent). NOT relied on: Art 7(1) and Art 29, which require only that policy be set 'in consultation with the Royal Government' - consultation is not approval; Art 9 grants operating autonomy. The law was amended as to Arts 14 and 57 by a law of 29 December 2006, which the source notes but whose text was not read.

QATAR (NOT settled - host blocked). The Qatar Central Bank Law No. 13 of 2012 is not reachable from this session. qcb.gov.qa fails TLS verification for curl ('SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate', the same failure mode as cbo.gov.om), and four WebSearches (including queries naming qcb.gov.qa and almeezan.qa) returned no qcb.gov.qa or almeezan.qa URL at all, so WebFetch could not be used - a constructed URL such as https://www.qcb.gov.qa/sites/default/files/qcblaw-en.pdf is refused for want of provenance, and that exact path also failed TLS under curl. Searches returned only secondary material (a Clifford Chance briefing PDF, Gulf Times and Peninsula articles). Needs a hand check of the QCB legislation page or almeezan.qa.

TAJIKISTAN (NOT settled). nbt.tj serves to curl, but it publishes no English text of the Law 'On the National Bank of Tajikistan'. Fetched https://www.nbt.tj/en/about/legislation.php (its 'Banking legislation' page): it names the Law 'On the National Bank of Tajikistan' and the Law 'On banks and banking activities' but links neither, in any language. https://nbt.tj/dmm/en/laws.php carries only one document, CFT_AML_Law.pdf. The only English PDF found on nbt.tj was https://www.nbt.tj/files/monetary_policy/COMMEETEE/en/EN_REGULATIONS.pdf, the Monetary Policy Committee regulations, which were read in full and contain no executive power: the NBT Chairman chairs the MPC, MPC decisions bind after his signature, and no minister or government body appears. Three searches found no official English text (only base.spinform.ru, a Russian commercial aggregator marked 'no longer in force').

BRUNEI (NOT settled as a statutory record - lead attached). The text of the Brunei Darussalam Central Bank Order, 2010 could not be found. bdcb.gov.bn is a JavaScript site with no crawlable legislation index (/regulatory returns a shell page; /regulatory/legislation and /about-us/legislation return 404), and agc.gov.bn returned 404 for every probed path. Fourteen PDFs on cms.bdcb.gov.bn surfaced by four searches were downloaded and identified: the Constitution, the Banking Order 2006, the International Banking Order 2000, the Islamic Banking Act, the Syariah Financial Supervisory Board Act, the Payment and Settlement Systems (Oversight) Act, corporate-governance guidelines, notices, and annual reports - none is the Order. What was found, and is worth a hand check: BDCB's own announcement of 21 October 2025 (https://cms.bdcb.gov.bn/storage/uploads/publications/17612898871704650.pdf) states that His Majesty the Sultan 'has consented to the appointment of BDCB's Board of Directors members' and lists them - the Chairman is the serving Minister of Primary Resources and Tourism, the Deputy Chairman the Deputy Minister of Finance and Economy, and the other members are the Deputy State Mufti, the Permanent Secretary (Wawasan) of the Prime Minister's Office, the Permanent Secretary (Economy, Trade and Industry) of the Ministry of Finance and Economy, the Solicitor General, and BDCB's Managing Director. BDCB's 2024 and 2025 audited financial statements confirm the bank was established on 1 January 2011 under section 3(1) of that Order. No record filed, because the brief asks for statutory provisions and the Order's text was never read.

MACAO (NOT settled - host unreachable). Both Macao gazette hosts are unreachable from this session's egress proxy: bo.io.gov.mo:443 and images.io.gov.mo:443 each return 'connect_unreachable (the host is allowed for this session, but the egress proxy could not connect to it)'. Two searches produced no amcm.gov.mo URL for the AMCM statute. Needs a hand check from a network that can reach io.gov.mo.

records.summary: Bahrain's Central Bank of Bahrain and Financial Institutions Law, promulgated by Law No. (64) of 2006 of 6 September 2006 and in force the day after publication, keeps the executive over the bank by its own terms: Article 5 puts all seven members of the Board of Directors, one of them a representative of the Ministry of Finance, in office by Royal Decree for renewable four-year terms, and the appointing Decree names the Chairman and Vice Chairman; Article 10 appoints the Governor, who is of ministerial rank, by Royal Decree for a renewable five-year term; and Article 173 has the Minister monitor the bank's adherence to 'the general economic policy of the Kingdom' and, where the Minister finds a conflict and the Board insists on its opinion, refer that conflict to the Cabinet, which resolves it by an order issued within thirty days. This is a standing statutory arrangement with no end date and no episode attached to it.
records.source_title: Law No. (64) of 2006 with respect to promulgating the Central Bank of Bahrain and Financial Institutions Law (consolidated English text, Legislation & Legal Opinion Commission, Kingdom of Bahrain)

records.summary: Oman's Banking Law, issued by Royal Decree 114/2000 of 13 December 2000 and effective on its publication in Official Gazette No. 685 of 16 December 2000, places the Central Bank of Oman under the head of state who is also the executive: Article 8(b) and Article 11(a) have all seven governors of the Board appointed by His Majesty the Sultan for five-year terms, with the Sultan designating which of them is Chairman and which Deputy Chairman, and Article 9 reserves one of those seats to a representative of the Ministry of Finance; Article 21(a) appoints the bank's Executive President by Royal Decree; Article 41(a) provides that 'the par value of the Rial Omani shall be determined from time to time by His Majesty the Sultan'; and Article 31 lets the Board set the external reserve ratio only subject to the Sultan's approval. This is a standing statutory arrangement with no end date and no episode attached to it.
records.source_title: The Banking Law, Royal Decree No. 114/2000 (English text published by the Central Bank of Oman)

records.summary: Cambodia's Law on the Organization and Conduct of the National Bank of Cambodia, promulgated on 26 January 1996, gives the executive the bank's leadership and part of its currency power: Article 13 provides that the Governor and the Deputy Governor are 'appointed, replaced and dismissed by a royal decree on the recommendation of the Royal Government', stating no grounds that must be met for a dismissal, and that the other Board members are appointed, replaced and dismissed by sub-decree; Article 12(1) seats on the seven-member Board both a representative of the Ministry of Economy and Finance and a representative of the head of the Royal Government; and Article 45 bars the bank from withdrawing or calling in currency without the Royal Government's consent. Policy itself is set by the Board, which Articles 7(1) and 29 require only to consult the Royal Government. This is a standing statutory arrangement with no end date and no episode attached to it.
records.source_title: Law on the Organization and Conduct of the National Bank of Cambodia (English text, National Committee for Sub-National Democratic Development library, Royal Government of Cambodia)
